definition: Cross-Region Replication copies objects to another Region for compliance, latency, or disaster recovery. Same-Region Replication aggregates logs or syncs accounts. Both need versioning on source and destination.
Only new objects replicate; S3 Batch Replication handles existing or failed ones. Version deletes and chained replication never replicate. Need a 15-minute SLA? Use Replication Time Control.
Infrequent-access class kept in a single Availability Zone, cheaper than Standard-IA, with retrieval fees and a 30-day minimum. Remember: only for re-creatable data, like secondary backup copies.
Instant Retrieval: milliseconds, 90-day minimum. Flexible Retrieval: 1 minute to 12 hours, 90-day minimum. Deep Archive: 12 to 48 hours, 180-day minimum, lowest cost.

High-performance class using directory buckets in one Availability Zone you choose, for consistent single-digit millisecond latency. Remember: put compute in the same zone; data is not multi-AZ resilient.
Automatically moves each object between access tiers based on its usage, for a small per-object monitoring fee and no retrieval fees. Remember: unknown or changing access patterns.
S3 events go directly to SNS, SQS standard queues, or Lambda. Use EventBridge for advanced filtering, many targets, and archive and replay. Remember: FIFO queues are not direct targets.
At least 3,500 write and 5,500 read requests per second per partitioned prefix, with unlimited prefixes. Spread keys across prefixes. Remember: SSE-KMS may hit KMS quotas first.
Multipart upload splits an upload into parallel parts, recommended over 100 MB and required over 5 GB. Byte-range fetches parallelize downloads or read just part of an object.
The requester, not the bucket owner, pays for requests and data downloaded; the owner still pays for storage. Requesters must be authenticated AWS identities, never anonymous.

term: Forcing HTTPS on an S3 bucket
definition: Add a bucket policy that denies any request where aws:SecureTransport is false, so every request must use HTTPS. Remember: encryption in transit is enforced with a bucket policy.
You send your own key with every request over HTTPS; S3 encrypts, then discards the key. Since April 2026, new buckets have SSE-C disabled until you turn it on.
WORM protection that needs versioning. Compliance mode: nobody, even root, can delete or shorten retention. Governance mode: permitted users can override. Legal hold: no end date until removed.
Locks a WORM policy on a legacy Glacier vault so it can never change. The vault service closed to new customers in December 2025, so use S3 Object Lock instead.
Temporary link carrying its creator's permissions to download or upload one object. Console links last up to 12 hours; CLI or SDK links up to 7 days.
Bucket rule letting a web page from one origin request objects from a bucket on another origin. Remember: configure CORS on the bucket being requested, not the site's bucket.
Rugged device for offline transfer when moving data online would take over a week. Imports land in S3, not Glacier. Closed to new customers since November 2025.
Parallel file system for HPC and machine learning with sub-millisecond latency. Links to S3 to read objects as files and write results back. Scratch is temporary; Persistent is replicated.
FSx for NetApp ONTAP speaks NFS, SMB, and iSCSI, ideal for NetApp migrations. FSx for OpenZFS speaks NFS only, for ZFS or Linux workloads. Both offer snapshots and instant clones.
S3 File Gateway: NFS or SMB files saved as S3 objects. Volume Gateway: iSCSI block volumes backed up as EBS snapshots. Tape Gateway: virtual tapes for existing backup software.
DataSync: scheduled, agent-based copies from NFS, SMB, or HDFS into S3, EFS, or FSx, keeping metadata. Transfer Family: managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP, or AS2 endpoints into S3 or EFS.
